title: Binomial presentation and coefficient derivation for a degree-p extended generic formal fibre
statement: Let k be a field of prime characteristic p, n,m nonnegative, A=k[[x_1,...,x_n]][y_1,...,y_m] [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] [def-weil-polynomial-ring], q a prime of A, K=κ_A(0) its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and C the maximal-ideal-adic completion of A_q [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let L/K be a finite purely inseparable field extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], M an intermediate field finite purely inseparable over K, and z in L such that M(z)=L, z^p lies in M, and [L:M]=p. Put F=K tensor_A C and R=M tensor_K F [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then there are f in R and an absolute derivation D:R -> R (additive and satisfying Leibniz) such that D(f) is a unit and R[Z]/(Z^p-f) is isomorphic as a ring to L tensor_K F. No regularity hypothesis or conclusion is imposed.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR, proof, finite-model and derivation paragraphs (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07PR)

proof.text: The power-series coefficient ring is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete]. The regular-local localization theorem [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] makes it a regular ring. Mathlib MvPolynomial.isRegularRing_of_isRegularRing makes A regular. Thus every prime localization of A is normal by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal]; [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-of-local-normal] makes the domain A integrally closed.

Choose a finite A-subalgebra B of M with fraction field M by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-subalgebra-fraction-field]. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian]. The given z and degree show that its minimal polynomial over M has degree p, so f=z^p in M is not a pth power: otherwise characteristic p implies z equals its pth root in M and the degree is one. Write f=b/s with s nonzero in B. Replacing z by sz and f by s^(p-1)b in B preserves M(z)=L and degree p, and a pth root of the new f would give a pth root of the old f by division by s.

Set E=B[Z]/(Z^p-f). The monic-quotient free basis theorem [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] gives basis 1,Z,...,Z^(p-1), so E is finite free over B and finite over A. Evaluation in L is injective because a relation of degree less than p contradicts the minimal polynomial degree p. Its fraction field is L, and E tensor_B M is M[Z]/(Z^p-f), hence L.

Normality of A and [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-integral-prime-unique] give a unique prime r of B over q. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-radicial-prime-unique-degree-p] to E: every pth power comes from B and there is a unique prime t over r. Hence t is the only prime of E over q. For a prime of the localization E tensor_B B_r, its contraction in B lies inside r; taking pth powers puts its contraction in E inside t. Thus this localization is local with maximal ideal t and equals E_t.

B_r is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Its local monic quotient is E_t, so [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-quotient] identifies completion(E_t) with completion(B_r)[Z]/(Z^p-f), compatibly with both coefficient and E maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension] to A -> B and A -> E at q. Each finite product has a single factor by prime uniqueness. Tensor the first comparison with M and the second with L. Tensor associativity, exchange of factors and quotient base change identify R=M tensor_K F with completion(B_r) tensor_B M and the L-fibre with R[Z]/(Z^p-f). Compatibility in the completion lemmas ensures these identifications use the same f.

The power-series base is Noetherian complete local by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete]. B is finite type over this base, since it is finite over its polynomial algebra A. The non-pth-power f is detected by an absolute derivation of B by [lem-weil-pbc-derivation-nonzero-on-non-pth-power]. Extend it to B_r, its completion and the localization completion(B_r) tensor_B M using [lem-weil-pbc-derivation-extends]. Compatibility with B says its value on f is the image of the nonzero element D(f) of M, so is a unit even if the fibre is the zero ring. Transport f, the derivation and the binomial quotient along the preceding ring equivalences. These give exactly the stated witnesses; regularity has not been assumed or concluded.
